entries.title: Daniel 2:2
segments: Chaldeans; that is, astrologers, because the Chaldeans were preeminent in this science.

entries.title: Daniel 2:4
segments: In Syriac; that is, in the Chaldee tongue.  From
the original is in the Chaldee language.

entries.title: Daniel 2:8
segments: Gain the time; improve to your own advantage the opportunity afforded you by my forgetfulness.  Compare

entries.title: Daniel 2:9
segments: Till the time be changed; probably, till my kingdom passes into other hands.  Compare
.  This is the language of jealousy and suspicion, as if the wise men forsaw calamity coming upon him which they refused to declare.

entries.title: Daniel 2:10
segments:
vv 10-11. 
 
None but the living God can reveal the secrets of the future.  All who pretend to a supernatural knowledge of coming events from any other source, are deceivers; and when their power is once fairly tested, they will, like the Chaldean magicians, be confounded and put to silence.

entries.title: Daniel 2:12
segments: It is natural that he who makes unreasonable demands of his fellow men should manifest unreasonable rage at their inability to comply with his desires.

entries.title: Daniel 2:13
segments: The angry man is sure to act in such a way as will hurt others without benefiting himself.

entries.title: Daniel 2:14
segments: The truly wise man is known by his ability to calm the excitement of the passionate, and thus gain for himself and them time for prudent action.

entries.title: Daniel 2:17
segments: vv 17-18. In times of great difficulty and danger, we should seek not only the counsels, but also the intercessory prayers of our fellow believers.

entries.title: Daniel 2:19
segments: God does not disappoint the hopes of his people when they seek him unitedly in fervent and believing prayer.

entries.title: Daniel 2:20
segments:
vv 20,23. 
 
God is the only source of wisdom and power.  In all the gifts and endowments which any of his servants possess, he should be gratefully recognized, and all the glory of them be ascribed to him alone.

entries.title: Daniel 2:31
segments:
vv 31-43. 
 
To the eternal mind of God, the whole history of the world lies open from the beginning to the end; and it is proceeding from age to age, in accordance with his infinitely holy and wise purposes, always in subordination to his glorious plan of redemption through Jesus Christ.

entries.title: Daniel 2:34
segments: Cut out; of the mountain,

. 
 
  Without hands; by no human agency.

entries.title: Daniel 2:38
segments: Thou art this head; that is, the kingdom over which thou reignest, and which is represented in thy person.

entries.title: Daniel 2:39
segments:
Another kingdom; the Persian, founded by Dyrus. 
 
  Inferior to thee; that is, in splendor. 
 
  Another third kingdom; the Grecian empire, of which Alexander was the founder.

entries.title: Daniel 2:40
segments: The fourth kingdom; this kingdom is at the beginning "strong as iron;" afterwards it is "partly strong, and partly broken,"

; it is on its decline when the God of heaven sets up his kingdom, for the stone cut out of the mountain without hands smites it on its feet of iron and clay, and it is the last great monarchy that oppresses the world.  All these characters point to the Roman empire, which would not be omitted in a comprehensive view, like this, of the future history of the world.  See notes on

entries.title: Daniel 2:41
segments: Divided; in character; that is, "partly strong, and partly broken,"

entries.title: Daniel 2:43
segments:
They shall mingle themselves; the native stock of this iron kingdom. 
 
  With the seed of men; with men of another sort, making a mixture that cannot be united into one whole.  According to some, the reference is to the Roman custom of giving to the nations whom they conquered the privilege of citizenship, thus making the empire a medley of different people, with different languages, ideas, and customs.  We may better, perhaps, understand these words of the mixture of the northern nations, who conquered Rome in the fourth and following centuries, with the old inhabitants of the empire.  Out of this grew a number of kingdoms that could never unite into one whole, and yet they constituted a continuation of the old Roman empire.  See notes on

entries.title: Daniel 2:44
segments:
Set up a kingdom; that called in the New Testament "the kingdom of heaven," of which Christ is the head. 
 
All the empires which human hands have established shall be destroyed; but the kingdom which God has established "without hands" shall increase continually, till the earth is filled with its glory and blessedness.

entries.title: Daniel 2:46
segments: Worshipped Daniel--sweet odors; we have no reason to think that Daniel failed to protest against any honors paid to him as a divine person, or as one who was the dwelling-place of deity.

entries.title: Daniel 2:48
segments: It is the part of wisdom to advance to stations of power and influence those who have given proof of their ability to fulfil in a proper manner the weighty responsibilities connected with them.

entries.title: Daniel 2:49
segments:
In the gate of the king; that is, in the gate of the king's palace, where public business was transacted.  He was plainly the chief minister of state. 
 
The good man in the office will desire and seek to surround himself by those who are of like character with himself.
